items: CBI is NOT a statutory body created by an Act of Parliament; it receives its powers from the Delhi Special Police Establishment (DSPE) Act, 1946.

The Director of CBI is appointed by a statutory committee consisting of the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition (or Leader of the single largest opposition party in Lok Sabha), and the Chief Justice of India (or a Supreme Court Judge nominated by CJI).
CVC submits its annual report directly to the President of India, who lays it before each House of Parliament.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Lokpal is a statutory anti-corruption ombudsman established under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, holding jurisdiction over public servants including the Prime Minister under specified conditions.
The Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) was established in 1964 following the recommendations of the Santhanam Committee and was granted statutory status in 2003.
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) is a non-statutory body deriving its investigative powers from the Delhi Special Police Establishment (DSPE) Act, 1946.
While Lokpal functions as an overarching inquiry authority and CVC supervises vigilance administration, CBI serves as the primary executive investigating agency.
